name: Essbase
tagline: Oracle's multidimensional OLAP cube server, the long-time engine behind financial planning and reporting.
description: Essbase is a multidimensional database for OLAP cubes, first released by Arbor Software in 1992, merged into Hyperion in 1998 and owned by Oracle since 2007. Data lives in cubes of dimensions and hierarchies such as accounts, time, entity and scenario, stored either as block storage (BSO), suited to write-back and complex calculation scripts used in budgeting, or aggregate storage (ASO), suited to very large, sparse read-mostly cubes, with a hybrid mode combining both. Users query it with MDX and MaxL, through Excel via Smart View, or through Oracle Analytics. It also sits underneath Oracle's EPM planning products. Oracle remains invested: Essbase 26.1, branded 26ai, shipped in August 2026 as the long-term release after 21c, with independent and OCI Marketplace deployments and a built-in MCP server.

pricing.notes: Licensed through Oracle (processor or named-user metrics); OCI Marketplace stacks run on customer-paid OCI compute.

scale.notes: Scales up on large servers; ASO cubes handle very high dimensionality, but there is no shared-nothing scale-out.

strengths: Purpose-built for hierarchical financial models: allocations, consolidations, currency conversion and what-if scenarios
Write-back cubes let planners enter data directly from Excel via Smart View
Two storage engines (BSO for calculation, ASO for huge sparse cubes) plus hybrid mode
Three decades of finance-team adoption and Oracle EPM integration
Actively developed: 26.1 (Aug 2026) adds MCP access and new platform support
weaknesses: Specialised cube modelling and calc-script skills are scarce and costly
No horizontal scale-out; large BSO calculations can take hours
Expensive Oracle licensing and lock-in to Oracle tooling
Poor fit for ad-hoc SQL analytics compared with modern columnar warehouses
useCases: Corporate budgeting, forecasting and financial consolidation
Management and profitability reporting from Excel
Back end for Oracle EPM / Hyperion Planning applications
What-if scenario modelling over hierarchical dimensions
